title: Where did it go?
text: {~Looking back|Doing the accounts one evening|A friend asks, innocently}, you try to work out where that sudden money went. {~There is a pattern, and it isn't flattering.|It's both better and worse than you thought.}

choices.label: Go through it line by line

outcomes.text: The honest accounting hurt for an evening. I came out of it a more careful person.
I found a subscription I'd forgotten for three years. The ledger was a bruise.
Some money is for living. I raised a glass to the afternoon it bought me.
Telling myself it was worth it worked for a week.

choices.label: Resolve to save the next one

outcomes.text: I opened a savings account the next morning and fed it a little every month.
I resolved. Then the next windfall came and went the same way.

title: About that tip
text: {~A newspaper article|A podcast|Your own bank statement} reminds you of the tip you {~took|passed on|half-listened to} {~a few|some} years ago.

choices.label: Check what it would have been

outcomes.text: It would have been a lot. I looked at the number for a long minute and closed the tab.
It would have been worth nothing. I felt briefly clever and then very lucky.

choices.label: Message the person who gave it

outcomes.text: We laughed about it. They'd lost money too, and had been too embarrassed to tell me.
They'd moved on and didn't remember the tip at all.
There's no use in the fortune you didn't make. I let it go like a train.
I let it go, and it let go of me about a year later.

title: Your name in the building
text: {~A former tenant|Someone in the building|A new tenant} mentions what they've heard about you as a landlord. {~It isn't what you expected.|It's been going round for a while.}

outcomes.text: It was fairer than I'd feared, and more specific than I'd like. I changed one habit.
It was unfair, and partly true, which is the worst combination.
I wrote a note to the building. People remembered it kindly.
Setting the record straight made it a bigger story than it had been.
I fixed the thing they'd complained about before they asked. It paid off over several years.
The gesture was misread as guilt, and a little was taken advantage of.

title: The envelope
text: A brown envelope arrives. {~It's about the thing from a couple of years ago.|You'd forgotten all about it.|You open it with your thumb under the flap and your heart under your tongue.}

outcomes.text: It took an afternoon and a phone call. It was nothing, and I felt like an adult.
It took an afternoon, and it was something. I paid it and felt slightly sick.
The drawer got fuller. In the end it never mattered.
The drawer got fuller. In the end it very much mattered.

choices.label: Ask a friend to read it

outcomes.text: They read it in twenty seconds and said 'ignore that one'. I could have kissed them.
They read it and went quiet. Then they helped me fix it.

title: The money question again
text: {~It comes up at dinner|It's mentioned in passing|Someone asks, casually}: the loan, or the gift, from a while back. Everyone is suddenly very interested in their glass.

outcomes.text: I said it plainly. The air cleared and we both felt better.
Saying it plainly made it a Thing. We didn't speak for a month.

choices.label: Forgive it, in so many words

outcomes.text: I said 'forget it'. They cried a little. It's the best money I've ever lost.
I said 'forget it', and meant it for about a year.
I changed the subject and nobody noticed.
I changed the subject and everybody noticed.

title: The night people still mention
text: {~Someone at a gathering|An old photo|A message out of nowhere} brings up that night. {~It's become a story.|They remember it better than you do.}

outcomes.text: I told it with the gestures. It's improved with the years, as these things do.
I told it and got a detail wrong. Someone corrected me, gently.
Modesty went over well. I was told I was 'refreshing'.
Modesty didn't land. People thought I was hiding something.
We did it again, smaller and better. It's now a tradition.
We tried to repeat it, and the magic stayed in the first one.

title: Next door, a year on
text: The {~noise|argument|barbecue} with the neighbour is ancient history now. {~Or it was, until this morning.|They've just knocked on the door.}

outcomes.text: They'd come about a parcel. We talked for twenty minutes on the step and it was lovely.
They'd come to complain again. I answered warmly and it didn't help.
Coolly was enough. They went away and something resolved itself.
Coolly started the feud again, with fresh enthusiasm.
I let it ring. They left a note, which was kind.
I let it ring. They left a note, which was not kind.

title: What the repair taught
text: The {~boiler|wall|roof} is still fine. You catch yourself {~knowing exactly what to do when something small goes wrong|explaining it to a friend with startling authority}.

outcomes.text: A friend borrowed my know-how and saved a fortune. They sent a bottle.
A friend ignored my advice and flooded their bathroom. I was kind about it.
I did the whole bathroom myself. It's slightly crooked and I adore it.
The bigger project ate a whole summer. Someone had to finish it for me.
A service contract, a yearly check, and sleep. Priceless.
The service contract turned out to cover nothing I needed.

title: A letter from the landlord
text: A letter from {~the agency|your landlord} arrives. {~It uses the word 'regarding'.|It's the third this year.}

outcomes.text: I read it twice. A small clause was in my favour and I used it.
I read it twice. It was exactly as bad as I thought.
A group of tenants told me it was illegal. It stopped.
The group said it was legal and annoying. I felt less alone.
I looked at four places and found one that made me feel hopeful.
I looked at four places and came home grateful for the one I had.

title: Whatever happened to your flatmate
text: {~A friend sends you a link|You see them across a street|A mutual friend tells you} about the person who shared your flat. {~Their life is nothing like you'd expect.|They are exactly who you thought they'd be.}

outcomes.text: We had a drink. The old arguments were funny from this distance.
We had a drink. We agreed that some people are meant for one flat.
I sent a thumbs-up and felt a clean, small kind of affection.
I wished them well and thought of the dishes.

choices.label: Tell the story of the flat

outcomes.text: The story of the flat got the loudest laugh of the dinner.
The story of the flat was funnier to me than to them.

title: The car story
text: At {~a dinner|a wedding|a pub} you tell the story of {~the car|the crash|the breakdown}. {~It's improved with the telling.|It's got a punchline now.}

outcomes.text: Straight is funnier than I'd have thought. People laughed in the right places.
Straight was dull. I cut it short.
A little became a lot, and the story acquired a goat.
Someone who was there corrected the goat.
Someone else told it, wrongly and brilliantly.
Someone else told it and got my part completely wrong.

title: Your old rival
text: {~On a professional network|At a conference|In the queue for coffee}, you meet the person you once competed with. {~They look well.|They look, to your surprise, tired.}

outcomes.text: It was the grown-up thing. They were visibly thrown, then touched.
It was the grown-up thing. They were suspicious.
Polite, brief, civil. We'll never be friends and nothing else needs saying.
Polite, brief, civil, and someone nearby clearly noticed it was loaded.
They did it, with an air of relief. Some rivalries are one favour from friendship.
They refused, with an air of triumph.

title: Your old boss
text: Your old boss {~sends a message|appears at an event|is mentioned in the news}. {~You haven't thought of them in years.|Everything about them comes back at once.}

outcomes.text: They remembered one thing I'd done that I'd forgotten. It was a kindness I hadn't known they'd noticed.
They wanted a favour. I did it, because I'm that kind of person.
A short reply was enough. They never wrote again.
A short reply was read as a snub, and that got around.
I let it lie. It felt like cutting a thread.
I let it lie, and wondered for a long time what it was about.

title: The company you left
text: {~The company you used to work for|Your old employer} is in the news. {~It isn't going well.|It's being bought.|It's doing better than it ever did with you.}

outcomes.text: I felt the relief of someone who left a sinking ship, and the guilt of one who left others on it.
I felt relief. It was a small, mean pleasure and I enjoyed it.
Three of them were glad to hear from me. One needed a job.
Nobody answered. They were all busy being scared.
I decided it wasn't my business, and it wasn't.
I decided it wasn't my business, and read about it every day for a week.

title: What they told you
text: {~A line|A piece of advice|A habit} you picked up from {~a mentor|someone senior} turns out to be the thing that gets you through today.

choices.label: Pass it on to someone junior

outcomes.text: They looked at me as if I'd given them a map. I remembered exactly how that felt.
They nodded politely and forgot it. Perhaps it takes ten years.
They wrote back at once. They remembered me, which was the best part.
The letter came back. They had moved, or worse.
It stayed a private advantage, and a quiet one.
It stayed private, and I thought about that selfishness at night.

title: A second call
text: {~The same recruiter|Another recruiter|An unexpected name on the screen} rings again, {~two years after the first time|with a different job and the same smile}.

outcomes.text: The offer was better than the last. I negotiated, and it was easier than I remembered.
The offer was the same, with a better title and a worse commute.
I declined again. The recruiter, for once, said 'good for you'.
I declined again, and a month later regretted it.
A friend got the job and cried. It was the best thing I did all year.
A friend got the job, and it didn't suit them. We still laugh about it.

title: The part you turned down
text: You hear that the {~role|record deal|contract} you passed on has gone to someone else. {~They're very good in it.|It did well.|It flopped, gloriously.}

outcomes.text: They were good. I sat in the dark and clapped for someone else's version of my life.
They were bad. I was ashamed of how pleased I was.
I stayed home and learned the lines of something else.
I stayed home and thought about it all night.
They wrote back warmly. It turned into a long correspondence.
They didn't reply, and I understood.

title: What being known costs
text: A stranger {~recognises you in a very private moment|knows something about you they shouldn't|says a thing that tells you how you look from outside}. {~You pretend not to mind.|It stays with you for days.}

choices.label: Take a break from the public

outcomes.text: A season in the country, a phone in a drawer. I returned a little more myself.
The break was read as a retreat, and the commentary was unkind.
I made it into a joke on my terms. They loved it.
I tried to make it a joke. It wasn't, and I'd shown that.
Silence cooled it. The next story took over.
Silence was read as guilt, and the story grew.

title: A young player asks
text: A young player {~at a clinic|after a match|in the car park} asks you what it was like. {~They're nervous.|They've watched your tapes.}

outcomes.text: I told them about the injuries and the loneliness and the joy. They listened like it was scripture.
I told them the truth, and saw their face fall. I tried to rescue it.
The highlights were exactly what they wanted. We both had a lovely afternoon.
The highlights rang hollow, and they could tell.

choices.label: Offer them a place to train

outcomes.text: They trained with me for a year and went on to great things. They still send photos.
They trained for a month and left. Not everyone sticks.

title: The voter remembers
text: At {~a fundraiser|a supermarket|a school event}, someone {~thanks|challenges|quotes} you on something you said {~at a debate|about a bill|about a donor}.

outcomes.text: Owning it won more respect than the original statement had.
Owning it cost me a donor and bought me a crowd.
I explained. They nodded slowly, and changed their mind.
I explained. They filmed it. The clip was not generous.
I'm good at smoothly. They never noticed.
I'm not as good at smoothly as I thought.

title: A debt that isn't money
text: A name from the old days {~turns up|calls|appears at a table}. They remember what you did, and what you didn't.

outcomes.text: A bright cafe, a long coffee. We talked around the point until it dissolved.
A bright cafe, and they weren't alone. I paid for everyone's coffee.
I paid it and it wasn't about the money. They nodded and the matter was closed.
I paid. It wasn't enough, and I learned how much would be.
I took a long trip and came back to a different set of problems. It worked.
I took a trip and they were waiting at the other end.

title: The studio comes back
text: {~The studio|A producer|Your agent} rings again, years after the last argument. {~They want something.|They sound almost humble.}

outcomes.text: The meeting was a revelation: they wanted me on my terms. I was smug for a week.
The meeting was the same argument in a better suit.
I made them wait a month. They improved the offer by a third.
I made them wait a month. They called someone else.

choices.label: Pass the opportunity to a friend

outcomes.text: A friend got a break and never forgot it.
A friend got a break and wasted it. I was surprised how much that stung.

title: A face from the service
text: Someone you worked with {~appears in a crowd|sits down at your table|sends a postcard with no name}. {~You both know what you used to do.|Neither of you says a word at first.}

choices.label: Greet them as an old friend

outcomes.text: We sat for an hour discussing nothing. It was the most intimate conversation I've had in years.
We greeted each other as old friends. Someone watched us do it.
Walking on felt like leaving a coat in a cold room.
Walking on, I noticed I was being followed, and was cheered by it.
I passed it. It was received. We never learned what it did.
I passed it, and it went to the wrong person.

title: Looking up
text: On a clear night, {~you stand in a garden|you're on a roof|you walk home}, looking up at where you used to {~work|train|live}.

choices.label: Take someone with you to look

outcomes.text: They looked up at a dot and I told them all of it. It was the best conversation of the month.
They looked up, and then at their phone. I forgave them.
The memories came in a quiet line. I was lucky, and I knew it.
The memories came in a loud rush. I went indoors.
I booked something small and real. It cured the ache.
I planned a trip and never booked it. The plan was enough.

title: Brother, sister, years on
text: Your {~brother|sister|sibling} {~calls out of the blue|appears on the doorstep|writes a long email}. {~You haven't spoken properly in a while.|It's about something small, which is how you know it isn't.}

outcomes.text: We sat up all night in the kitchen. By morning we'd said everything.
We sat up all night and said only half of it. It was a start.
Short was enough. We'll finish it at Christmas.
Short was too short. I felt it afterwards.
I brought it up and we both laughed. It had been too small to hold for so long.
I brought it up and we argued for an hour. We were better afterwards.

title: The phone call
text: Your {~mother|father|parent} rings, {~as they always do on a Sunday|at an odd hour|with nothing in particular to say}.

outcomes.text: An hour about nothing. I learned a story I'd never heard about their youth.
An hour about nothing. They seemed lonelier than they sounded.
I went the next weekend. We fixed a gate and ate too much.
I planned a visit and cancelled it. They said they understood.
It went to voicemail. The message was warm, and made me feel worse.
It went to voicemail, and I called back that night. We talked for hours.

title: The child is grown
text: Your child {~says something that stops you|does something you didn't teach them|treats you, for a moment, like an equal}. {~You're startled by how much of you is in it.|You're startled by how little.}

outcomes.text: They said 'I know', then 'thanks'. I heard everything under it.
They said 'Mum, stop.' They smiled anyway.
They gave me an answer I'd not thought of. The student had become a teacher.
They gave advice I didn't want to follow. I thought about it for a week.
Watching them was the best part. They're their own person.
Watching them, I wished I could say it. I never did.

title: A conversation you've been avoiding
text: {~Late at night|On a long drive|Over the washing-up}, the subject of {~what you each want|the big decision|the thing you never discuss} finally comes up.

outcomes.text: It was frightening. It was also, by morning, a relief.
It came out wrong, and we spent three days recovering.
Listening revealed that we'd been afraid of the same thing.
Listening revealed a gap I hadn't known was there.
We agreed to talk on Sunday. On Sunday it was easier.
We agreed to talk on Sunday, then didn't. It sat between us.

title: The old crowd
text: Someone {~organises|suggests|just starts} a get-together with the old crowd. {~Half of them will turn up.|It's been far too long.}

outcomes.text: It took a train and a babysitter. It was worth every penny.
It took a train and a babysitter, and the evening was awkward. I'm glad I went.
An hour was enough to remember why we were friends.
An hour was the right length for how things are now.
The gift was passed round the table and I was toasted in absentia.
The gift arrived late and was a bit of an apology.

title: Wedding photos
text: Someone finds the {~wedding photos|album|video}. {~Everyone looks so young.|One of the guests isn't in the story any more.}

outcomes.text: We laughed at the hair. Somebody cried at the speeches.
We looked through them, and a few missing faces made it quiet.
I put them away for another time. It's a kindness to the day.
I put them away, and thought of them for a week.
Three people wrote back, moved. One had lost the original.
Nobody replied, but I know they were opened.

title: Their stories
text: A story from {~a grandparent|an elder|a relative} comes back to you, {~word for word|in their voice|at an odd moment}. {~You realise you're the only one who still has it.|You wonder who else remembers.}

outcomes.text: It filled four pages. I put them in the family box.
It filled four pages and I lost them. I remember it, mostly.
The child listened with their whole face. The story lives on.
The child asked if there was a screen version. I laughed until I wept.
It's mine, and I like having it.
It's mine. When I go, it goes. I think about that more than I admit.

title: The animal knows
text: Your {~pet|animal|stray-turned-resident} does something that {~makes you laugh until you cry|makes your heart stop|tells you they've been listening all along}.

outcomes.text: The photograph is on the fridge. It's the best thing in the flat.
The photograph is blurred. The memory is perfect.
A new bed, a long walk, and a snack. They have regard for me now.
A new bed, ignored in favour of the box it came in.
Everyone has a pet story. We traded them all evening.
Nobody wanted another pet story. I kept going.

title: Whatever happened to them
text: {~Out of nowhere|On a feed|At a funeral} you hear about someone from school. {~You haven't thought about them in years.|They were the one you'd never have guessed.}

outcomes.text: Their life was a surprise, a good one. I smiled for the rest of the day.
Their life was a surprise, a hard one. I sat quietly.
They replied in minutes. It was as if no time had passed.

title: The thing you were good at
text: You come across {~a drawing|a trophy|an old project} from {~childhood|school|years ago} that shows the thing you once were good at. {~It was never a career.|You'd forgotten how much you loved it.}

outcomes.text: It was rusty. By the third evening it was a joy.
It was rusty. I stopped after a week, with a bruised ego.
The child had a gift too. We spent a summer of evenings on it.
The child was bored in ten minutes. I laughed.
It hangs in the hall. People ask about it and I tell them.
It hangs in the hall, and the frame outshines it.

title: Your first job, remembered
text: {~The smell of a kitchen|A uniform in a shop window|A phrase from a customer} takes you back to your first job. {~You were so young.|You were so tired, and so proud.}

choices.label: Tell a young person about it

outcomes.text: They listened, shocked at the wages. I felt about a hundred years old.

It was still there, smaller. The manager remembered my name.
It was a phone shop now. I stood outside, grinning.
A habit for life: I tip generously and mean it.

title: The thing nobody knew

text: Years after the exam, you find yourself {~in a situation where it would have helped|explaining something you learned for it|dreaming that you're sitting it again}.

title: The habit that stuck

title: What your body said

title: Someone remembers
text: {~A stranger|Someone you barely know|A person in a shop} says, 'You're the one who...' and tells a story about a small thing you did. {~You'd completely forgotten it.|You remember it differently.}

text: {~At a barbecue|On a train|In a quiet moment}, you hear yourself telling the story of that day at work again. {~It's got better with age.|It has a shape now.}

text: {~At a family dinner|Out with friends|Alone at home}, you notice how you're holding your glass. {~It's a habit you've watched for a while.|Someone else has noticed too.}
